methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target distributed skill-building in a non-metro region, representing grassroots peer-network learning that could prevent Hampton Roads from falling into the widening gap scenario.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ investment in AI data center infrastructure concentrating 200 jobs in Henrico reinforces Richmond's position as an emerging tech hub, but signals capital-intensive rather than distributed capability development.

signals.title: AI Boom Drives Fight Over Electric Bills as D.C., Virginia and Maryland Clash Over Data Centers - The Washington Informer
signals.signal_reading: Regional conflict over electric bills driven by NoVA's data center boom reveals how concentrated AI infrastructure deployment creates resource competition that may actually inhibit broader distribution across Virginia.

signals.title: Virginia should make AI adoption strengthen the career ladder | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Guest column advocating for AI adoption to strengthen career ladders signals policy awareness that shallow platform adoption alone won't build workforce capability—suggesting intentional investment in deep skill development may be gaining traction.

signals.title: Why this Virginia Tech professor says don't use AI for medical advice - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech professor warning against AI medical advice highlights the risk of shallow platform-based adoption where users lack deep understanding to critically evaluate AI outputs—a cautionary signal about distributed but superficial engagement.
